subtype: Approach: sets a device so strict that it backfires [Pitfall]
passage:
Friday, 9:30 pm. Well, that plan is dead. On Monday I set a blocker to lock every app on my phone, all day, no exceptions. No messages, no maps, no bank. I thought: cold turkey, total focus. Today at eleven, Ishita sent a photo of the client's signed form on the work chat and asked me to forward it within ten minutes. My phone would not open the chat. I hunted for a way round it, panicked, deleted the blocker altogether, and still sent the form twenty minutes late. Now everything is open again and I scrolled for an hour tonight. The rule was too strict. It never made room for the one app I actually need.

Naveen

qa.a: Naveen could set a lighter lock that blocks only the distracting apps and keeps the work chat open.

qa.a: Ishita may have felt anxious about the deadline and puzzled about why Naveen was unreachable.
